conviction_note: The evidence balances. The stock lost about 10% in five sessions as the Anthropic IPO (first trade 2026-11-19) unwound Zoom's role as a proxy for it, which lowers the bar. Against that, puts are bid (skew +16 vol points), the peer read is mixed (RingCentral raised, Five9 fell 19.8% on an AI-cost EPS cut) and the known 2H headwinds (white-label churn, flat Online) are already in the guide. p_up is 51 on a scale of 8.0, so the scaled number is +0.16 against an impact_sum of +0.30; both are close to zero, and that is the honest read. Search incomplete, so neither number should rank.
bar: The company's Q3 FY27 guide is revenue $1.275-1.280B and non-GAAP EPS $1.46-1.48, with non-GAAP operating income $510-515M (Q2 FY27 release, 2026-08-25: https://finviz.com/news/385449/zoom-communications-reports-financial-results-for-the-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027). Earnings Whispers' preview of 2026-11-15 puts consensus at $1.28B and $1.49 EPS, with a whisper of $1.55 (https://finviz.com/news/422873/zooms-enterprise-inflection-faces-its-next-test-as-white-label-churn-and-ai-costs-build). Benzinga's quote page shows an EPS estimate of $1.39, which disagrees and is probably a GAAP or stale figure (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZM/charts). The Q4 revenue guide implied by the FY guide of $5.085-5.095B is about $1.291-1.301B (FY less Q1 $1,239.0M, Q2 $1,277.2M and the Q3 guide midpoint). In Q2, revenue beat the top of its guide by $7.2M (1,277.2 against 1,270), which would put Q3 at about $1.287B, +0.5% over the $1.28B consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.9% of float, roughly 5.5M shares, at the 2026-11-13 settlement, with 2.3 days to cover and falling (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/zm/summary). Massive had 6.24M shares and 2.1 days on 2026-09-30. This is not a crowded short and there is no squeeze mechanism. Baseline skew is +16.04 vol points (25-delta put over call), so downside is paid. Put/call OI is 1.01, the event-implied move 7.04% (straddle 8.7%), the 5-day run-up -10.37%, the 20-day -12.07%, and the stock sits 22.9% below its 52-week high. Insiders made 92 open-market sales and 0 purchases in six months; the CEO made 40 sales totalling about $17.2M, probably under a plan (Quiver, 2026-11-19).

findings.finding: ZM fell from $99.80 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-15) to $86.21 at the seal, -10.4% in 5 sessions. Over that week Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 (2026-11-18, about a $1.5T valuation), first traded 2026-11-19 and closed day one at $97.17. Zoom's stake was carried at about $3.13B at a $965B valuation on 2026-07-31, on a $51M cost plus about $301M added. Quiver (2026-11-19) calls ZM's slide that week positioning, not a company-specific setback, so the drop looks like holders unwinding Zoom as an Anthropic proxy once the direct share traded. At the IPO valuation the stake is about $5B or more against a market cap near $26B, so the core business is cheaper going into the print than it was a week ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ZM moved on Anthropic headlines: +9.9% to $111.62 on the IPO filing in June 2026 (Stocktwits/Invezz, 2026-06-01). Q2 FY27 GAAP EPS of $5.15 included a $1.61B strategic-investment gain, and the stock still fell 7.03% on core Online weakness. The market sizes ZM on the core, not on the gain line.
findings.why_not_priced: The unwind is itself the pricing. What is not priced is any reversal: if proxy money had already come back, the 5-day run-up would not be -10% with the core business unchanged since 2026-08-25 (no 2.02 or 7.01 8-K since 2026-09-02). There is no dated mechanism that closes the gap inside the window beyond the print itself, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Quiver, 2026-11-19 (https://quiverquant.com/news/Zoom%2BCommunications%2BSlips%2Bas%2BInvestors%2BWeigh%2BBroader%2BTech%2BWeakness%2Band%2Ba%2BNear-Term%2BEarnings%2BCatalyst), an AI-generated piece, attributes the drop to AI-valuation sentiment around the Anthropic IPO. The stake values come from CryptoBriefing, 2026-09-20 (https://cryptobriefing.com/zoom-anthropic-ipo-stake-gains/), citing the 10-Q.

findings.finding: RingCentral, the closest UCaaS peer, reported on 2026-10-22, after Zoom last spoke. Subscriptions revenue was $653M, +6.0% y/y and above the top of its guide, the fourth straight quarter of acceleration. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.33 against $1.27 consensus, and full-year revenue and FCF guidance were raised. That points to stable to improving enterprise UCaaS demand in Zoom's Aug-Oct quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On ZM's own enterprise line, Q2's 7.8% enterprise growth (best in three years) still sold off 7% because Online was weak. In Q1 (+9.19%) enterprise and NDE improved alongside a buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is a month old and the sell-side Q3 notes since then (Citi 11/17, Rosenblatt and BTIG 11/18, per Quiver) had it. It is a peer read, not a Zoom number, and it does not reach the white-label churn or Online lines.
findings.independence: This is a different company and source from the other findings. Five9's print (next finding) cuts the other way on margins.

findings.finding: Five9, a contact-center peer and competitor for Zoom Contact Center, reported on 2026-11-05. Revenue was +13%, above its guide, and AI revenue was about 17% of subscription. But it lowered FY non-GAAP EPS to $3.17-3.21 on AI investment and the Level AI acquisition, and the stock fell 19.8%. That is a live template for punishing AI-driven margin dilution. Zoom's own Q2 non-GAAP gross margin (79.1%) and operating margin (40.0%) already slipped on AI usage and the Common Room acquisition.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 raised FY non-GAAP EPS to $6.08-6.12 even as margins slipped, and the stock still fell 7.03%. There is no clean precedent for a Zoom margin-guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the bid puts (skew +16) are consistent with it. It is a peer read on how the market treats AI margins, not evidence that Zoom will cut, and Zoom's Q3 operating income guide of $510-515M on $1,277.5M revenue (about 40%) holds margin flat. It is sized small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Zoom's own Q2 margin slippage is in the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-15 (https://finviz.com/news/422873/zooms-enterprise-inflection-faces-its-next-test-as-white-label-churn-and-ai-costs-build).

findings.finding: Per the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-15, a white-label customer churn is a back-half headwind of roughly 40-60bp on Enterprise growth, from 7.8% in Q2. Enterprise is about 61% of revenue and is the line the stock trades on, alongside NDE at 99% and the market's wait for it to cross 100%. RPO grew 14% to about $4.5B, which offsets part of the headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Enterprise acceleration from 7.2% (Q1) to 7.8% (Q2) did not stop a -7.03% move in Q2. An enterprise deceleration has no clean recent precedent in the baseline's seven prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management disclosed it and it sits inside the Q3 guide and the unchanged constant-currency 2H outlook (Morgan Stanley via Reuters/finviz, 2026-08-26). The residual risk is that a visibly lower enterprise growth print reads as an inflection ending. It is sized net of the RPO growth (+14%) and the other 99% of enterprise.
findings.independence: Same document as the Online finding below. Morgan Stanley's 'unchanged cc 2H outlook' comment is at https://finviz.com/news/385567/zoom-beats-quarterly-forecasts-and-raises-full-year-outlook-but-shares-fall.

findings.finding: Online (about 38% of revenue, $489.7M, +0.6% y/y in Q2) had its full-year view cut from slight growth to flat. Online average monthly churn was 2.9%, flat y/y in Q2 and 3.0% in Q1, and Morgan Stanley flagged weaker Online top-of-funnel. Online is the line that sank Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27: Online +0.6% with weaker top-of-funnel, stock -7.03% despite a beat and raise. Q1 FY27: churn 3.0%, but the stock rose 9.19% on enterprise strength and a $1B buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is already in the FY guide. The Pro plan list price rise from $13.33 to $14.16 per user per month (about 2026-03-02, pricingsaas) supports Online ARPU, which partly offsets volume. The finding is small and could go either way.
findings.independence: The FY cut to flat comes from the Earnings Whispers preview, the same document as the white-label finding. The churn figures are from the company's Q1 and Q2 releases.

findings.finding: Buyback capacity: about $1.3B of authorization remained on 2026-07-31 after $360.5M was spent in Q2. Zoom added $1B in Q1 when about $0.6B remained. At Q2's pace, about $0.9-1.0B remains at Q3 end. FY FCF guidance is $1.78-1.82B, and the Anthropic stake, now publicly priced at about $5B or more but probably locked up for 6-12 months, adds visible balance-sheet value. A new authorization or a statement on monetizing the stake on the call is a possible capital-return catalyst.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (the $1B added authorization): +9.19%. That move was not on the buyback alone.
findings.why_not_priced: No one has announced a new authorization, so it is an inference about a decision management has not signalled. If the market expected one, the 5-day run-up would not be -10%. It is sized small because it is speculative.
findings.independence: The Q1 $1B add is at https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/05/22/why-zoom-stock-is-up-today/ (2026-05-22). The lockup expectation is from secondary sources, not a Zoom document.

findings.finding: The company sets its guide conservatively. Q2 revenue beat the top of guide by $7.2M ($1,277.2M against $1,265-1,270M), and non-GAAP EPS of $1.55 beat $1.48 consensus. Consensus for Q3 ($1.28B, $1.49) sits at the top of the guide, with a whisper of $1.55. A repeat of Q2's pattern gives about $1.287B and EPS of $1.53-1.56: a beat that is the base case and is priced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats both bought and sold: Q1 FY27 +9.19%, Q2 FY27 -7.03%, Q4 FY26 -11.58%, Q3 FY26 +9.85%. A beat alone does not set the sign; the Q4 guide and enterprise/Online mix do.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the whisper is above consensus. It is filed because the stock entering 10% lower makes the same beat land against a lower price than in August.
findings.independence: Same preview as the white-label and Online findings for consensus. The Q2 actuals are from the company release (finviz 385449).

baseline_tension: The negative findings (Five9's margin template, white-label churn, flat Online) agree with the +16 put skew and are therefore largely priced. The positives (proxy unwind lowering the bar, RingCentral's raise, buyback capacity) cut against the skew and the -10% run-up, but none comes with a mechanism the option market is missing, so p_up sits at 51.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside what the company already guided): white-label churn moved from -0.7 to -0.3 and Online from -0.4 to -0.2, because management disclosed both and both sit in the Q3 and FY guides.
Rule 9 (segment finding net of the rest): white-label churn sized net of RPO +14% and the rest of Enterprise.
Rule 5 (a proxy is filed small): Five9's margin read moved from -0.6 to -0.5 as a peer proxy, not a Zoom number.
Rule 1 (beats bought and sold alike in this name's history): the beat-pattern finding moved from +0.3 to +0.2.

Rule 2: the Anthropic item is filed as positioning, not one_off, because it acts through the share price and not through operating income. Sized from +0.5 to +0.4 because no mechanism closes the gap inside the window.
Rule 7: short interest checked (1.9%, 2.3 days, not crowded). The negatives agree with the skew, so they were not shrunk further.
